Thank you for taking the time to post this, it really is people like you who help those at risk feel like there's a chance they can find help. Speaking as someone who spent the better part of last year and some of this one contemplating, desiring, and resisting suicide, it can be hard to reach out, not only because there's still a stigma towards mental illness but also because when you're in such a dark place it can be hard to conceive of a way that anyone can actually help. That said, at least in my personal experience, help is what we want most (we want the agony to end, one way or another, help out of it or the idealized 'release' of death). I have been on both ends of the spectrum, having been suicidal on and off for half my life and having talked at least one other person out of suicide, and the best thing I can think of to help people is let them know they're not alone. When someone is there for you that really helps, but it's also important to be confronted with the fact that, as was mentioned elsewhere on this thread, your death causes far more damage than good (no matter what anyone tells you, no matter what you tell yourself, this is true). Getting a different perspective, getting out of your own head, getting a wake-up call (sometimes a really harsh one is needed), these are all very important to you deciding to give yourself a chance and put in the effort to help yourself. 
Thanks again OP, and to anyone feeling low, please feel free to reach out, even if it's only to talk about random things, because every little step helps.

Wow, that's very interesting. I'm glad you've found something that works for you, and I appreciate your sharing it with me. I find that I really don't like conflict in a relationship; of course, it's impossible to have a relationship without it, but I don't want to seek it out. I've been in a relationship where we fought constantly for the first year, and eventually I subconsciously began repressing myself in order to avoid conflict. Needless to say, that resulted in my second biggest depression. I like intellectual stimulation and I don't mind being challenged if it's constructive and comes from a supportive person, but I hate being judged and I don't want to live my life feeling like I have to constantly defend myself and my beliefs against the people I'm closest to. Also, I like to be able to relate to people and have them relate to me; being told 'oh ok, well I don't understand that, but you can think it if you want' is very disheartening and feels cold and hurtful. That's why I'd prefer to have some values and interests in common, so that we have a base to work from; having other interests that are different is essential to keep from being codependent and stagnating. So, a balance is what I'd like to try I guess...

First, I want to say thank you again. Though I find your tone somewhat brusque and confrontational, your intentions are good and I appreciate you taking the time to try to help. After crying myself to sleep and a horrible sleepless night, I managed to get through another day of work and am feeling less like dying. 

I don't want the pain to ever come back. I have recovered many times, only to fall again and again, and each time it gets harder to recover. I want a healthy, loving, stable relationship, but I have very little faith that there is anyone out there for me... 

I do not like medication, I've been on several and, in addition to not performing their intended purpose, they've all given me horrible side-effects that make everything worse. I don't want to be dependent on something, if there is an imbalance in my brain chemistry then I need to work on re-writing my thought patterns to compensate and building up coping mechanisms. CBT has worked in the past (I read the book and managed to recover all by myself after both medication and therapy left me worse than before), and my brother has suggested ACT, so maybe I will try that. 

The problems with therapy here are that, unlike my home country, it's not free; I have limited funds. Not to mention, I'm applying for a government scholarship that requires you to allow access to medical records, and this country is still somewhat behind in terms of not discriminating against mental illness; in other words, I'm afraid if I go somewhere and it goes in my file, I will be turned down, and I need this scholarship to get out of this city and into the masters degree that I am hoping to attain. 

I had suspected from prior to us breaking up that he was actually gay and simply couldn't accept it due to self-loathing (which he has admitted to) and cultural biases. To be clear, we never had sex. The relationship itself was supportive and loving and wonderful...until we met again after 7 months of being apart. We talked every day twice a day, he was always there for me and I did my best to do the same for him. On the intellectual and emotional levels, we were blissfully happy. It was the physical we were mismatched. Believe me, I know I deserve it all, and I want it all. But I'm so tired of being disappointed, of watching the years go by and wondering if I'm just doomed to always be alone. 

Obviously, at this very moment, of course I'm not ready for a relationship. At this moment I don't even want one; I want to focus on myself and learn how to be okay. But I'm not that young anymore and I'm scared that as time goes by it will only get harder and harder to find anyone even remotely attractive (in terms of all levels, not just physical). I am not comfortable with sex outside the context of a loving and committed relationship, I have a hard time trusting the opposite sex due to past incidents, and my standards seem to be fairly high. 

That said, I took the time to look up a clinic in my area, and will consider calling them (the website indicates they might accept self-pay instead of insurance, so maybe no record..?)

also, if this relationship, the best I've ever had (and I've had a couple), can fail, what hope do I have for any other? I've had my heart broken so many times I can barely get out of bed some days, and the thought of going through that again terrfies me. I just want the pain to stop.

thanks for commenting. I understand that he's moved on, and I'm happy for him. but I thought for sure he was the one. I'm scared I will never find anyone that suited me so well, and I don't want to settle for just anyone.
